title: Prologue
focus: the Prologue's sonnet and the ending foretold

teacherSummary.text: The Chorus speaks a sonnet: two households of equal rank in Verona break out in new violence from an old grudge; from them come a pair of 'star-cross'd lovers' whose deaths end their parents' strife. The play, the Chorus says, will show 'the two hours' traffic of our stage.'

context.history: Elizabethan plays sometimes opened with a Chorus or Prologue. The sonnet was the fashionable love-poem form of the 1590s; Shakespeare's own sonnets were circulating among friends by 1598.

significance: Telling the ending first turns the play from a story of what happens into a study of how and why, and makes every hopeful moment dramatically ironic.
